title: ProKeyboard

bodiesOfWork.title: Ergonomic iPhone keyboard concept
bodiesOfWork.summary: A self-initiated keyboard concept intended to adapt to cognitive and physical needs rather than require users to adapt to a fixed layout.

workingHypotheses: This may work better as an Impressions item or side-project note than as a full case study.

organisingIdea.statement: The keyboard should adapt to a person's cognitive or physical state instead of demanding that the person adapt to a fixed keyboard.

claims.statement: ProKeyboard is a self-initiated mobile-keyboard side project.
claims.notes: Project identity is consistent across both supplied sources.

claims.statement: The project explores a mobile keyboard intended to support focus, fluidity, accessibility, and neurodivergent users.
claims.notes: Confirm the current problem statement and preferred language around neurodivergence.

claims.statement: Explorations named in the old portfolio include subtle feedback loops, one-handed modes, adaptive keyboard shapes, and AI-enhanced prediction.
claims.notes: Confirm which explorations reached a working prototype.

claims.statement: The exploration used Gboard and iOS as reference points while questioning conventions inherited from early smartphone keyboards.
claims.notes: Needs a concrete example of what was retained or rejected from each reference.

claims.statement: The project was still being designed and prototyped when the 2025 CV and portfolio were produced.
A March 2025 project-status note describes ProKeyboard as ongoing but on hold, substantially ready to enter an iPhone build while waiting for stronger Xcode AI capability.
claims.notes: Confirm the current 2026 status and whether Xcode AI remains the blocker.

openQuestions.question: What exists today: sketches, a Figma prototype, coded keyboard, user test, or abandoned direction?
openQuestions.answer: By March 2025 the design was described as substantially ready for an iPhone build but on hold. The exact artefacts and current 2026 status remain unresolved.
